target_customer: Data teams at companies using warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks
problem: Data engineering and analysis work is slow, and AI agents lack trusted business definitions and lineage.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with open source Databench edition; Plus plan reported at $50 per month by one listing

founders.name: Tony Li
education: Yale, BS computer science and mathematics

founders.name: Andrew Tran
education: Yale, BS and MS computer science

competitors.name: Databricks Genie Code
competitors.what: Autonomous agent for data engineering and science

technical_complexity.rationale: Lineage, sandbox testing and agent workflows across many data tools.

defensibility.rationale: Lineage and knowledge base can lock in, but platform vendors ship competing agents.

market_need_then: Agentic data work was a hot 2026 category; Alkera cites benchmark results (vendor claim).

identity.logo: Identity built by design studio Artone in a two week sprint, per a listing
identity.mascot_or_character: Named demo agents Priya and Marcus
identity.visual_style: Geometric pattern system, light and dark wordmarks

branding.brand_signature: Open source Databench launched on Product Hunt 2026-10
branding.community_and_virality: Databench is Apache-2.0 on GitHub; community channels exist but few posts.

brand_strength.rationale: Professional identity and an open source product launch, but limited evidence of pull.

outcome_analysis: Alkera is a three person Yale founded Fall 2026 company. No outcome yet: the company is Active and a 2026 batch member; outcome searches found no acquisition, shutdown or layoff news. It competes with platform vendors' own agents, and its benchmark claims are self reported.
notes: Funding unverified: Caplight and EveryDev list about $500K from YC and Pareto Holdings; Dealroom shows $125k seed; aggregators only, so no round recorded. Batch listed as Summer 2026 by some sources, Fall 2026 in the directory.
